proposition.claim:
Quantization norm is at most sqrt(n)*smax^2/2 and subgroup excess risk admits the stated gradient/trace bound

Smaller groups have larger gradient norms/traces and hence suffer more quantization damage; lower bit-width exacerbates fairness gap

QAT excess loss is bounded by the displayed gradient/trace terms plus O(eta^2)

assumptions: Actual signed symmetric nearest-rounding quantizer, 0<s<1 and no clipping
Nonnegative smooth subgroup risks; first counterexample is convex and quadratic
Nonnegative convex quadratic group risks and positive finite group sizes
Convex C-infinity nonnegative fourth-power risk, identical groups/batches
Actual Eq11 update followed by AppendixA.6 requantization
Fixed b=4, initial global minimizer (1,-1,1/3), positive eta tending to zero
